body:
# the contributor audit: centroid graphs, level trimming, and source costs

This audit records bounded results. It does not certify a proof of OC.

## Maximum-volume centroid graph: PASS

The root read `candidate 7abc09359a7966ea` in full.
At an integer output of a positive convex combination, the direction space
of the Minkowski average is the sum of the source direction spaces. The
definition of the maximum intrinsic dimension forces these spaces to agree
before Brunn--Minkowski is used. Equality of the maximum volumes then forces
translations, and only after this step is centroid additivity invoked.

The projection Helly argument is valid because a common integer projection
has a unique point in the compact centroid hull. This uniqueness is essential:
projection does not commute with intersection for general fibers. The finite
counting argument retains closed-boundary mass, and transfer uses ordinary
Grunbaum within each counted intrinsic fiber. The resulting bound retains
M_max/M for unequal positive fiber volumes. The q=0, n=0, and d=0 cases are
included explicitly. No full OC inference follows from dropping that ratio.

## Equal-volume level trimming obstruction: PASS

The root read `candidate a1e40e6e6a2316e4`
and ran `supporting computation verify_equal_volume_level_trimming_obstruction.py`, which passed.
The four-corner convex-combination formula produces exactly the nine stated
integer intervals. At every 0<t<1, both diagonal pairs force different
centroid values at the integer center for every choice of length-t trims.
The central convexification requires length at least 1+2t. The comparison
3/22>1/8 is an actual original-body depth guarantee and correctly separates
the failed construction from OC.

## All-multiplicity source cost: PASS

The root read `candidate 61e9db32fbeb3f83` through
the complete fixed-alpha, global optimization, asymptotic, and Fenchel
arguments. The objective is s+r, with only one eta copy. The k-fold copy
appears only in the density whose centroid is tested.

The cap-tail root is concave by the cap Minkowski inclusion. Quantile
rearrangement gives the two leftmost occupied bands, and the simplex
construction attains every minimizing equality configuration. Compactness
and the perturbation excluding strict slack are valid at r=0, r=s, and the
other constraint boundaries. Reducing alpha to r preserves feasibility only
for the absolute objective; the normalized objective is treated separately.

Independently, the root derived the finite-k stationary parameterization
k=D(u)^d/Z(u)^(d+1), s=(Z/D)^d, r=u^d s, and the positive derivative of k(u).
The saved proof supplies the global derivative signs and endpoint threshold,
so the stationary equation is not being mistaken for global minimality.
The two scalar bounding roots give the fixed-d sharp asymptotic, and the
Fenchel comparison controls alpha in the normalized asymptotic. No claim
uniform in d is inferred from that limit.

The root also read `candidate 04fb8b3cc0275a7f` and ran
`supporting computation verify_all_multiplicity_interval_source.py`, which passed. Its feasible
endpoint clamping and the square-root thresholds agree with the root's
independent differentiation of the scalar objective.

## Brunn--Minkowski-mass dominated mean: PASS

The root read `candidate e4ccf81294305ade`.
Gaussian smoothing gives positive smooth bounded densities; triangular
conditional transports have positive diagonal derivatives. Holder applied
to those diagonal entries gives the full arithmetic Brunn--Minkowski mass,
not merely geometric-mean mass. The averaged triangular map is a global
diffeomorphism by successive monotone inversion. Tightness is obtained
from the fixed finite collection of converging marginals. Density domination
passes through compactly supported continuous test functions, and moments
are computed from the limiting compactly supported marginals, avoiding any
unjustified convergence of unbounded moments.

The residual centroid identity and its vector containments follow exactly.
The sharp own-fiber cap bound follows separately from Minkowski averages
of ordinary centroid caps; it does not require the dominated density itself
to be log-concave. The simplex and diamond examples establish only their
stated sharpness conclusions. This theorem bounds centroid-graph variation;
it supplies no weighted Helly principle for a graph with nonunique fibers.

## Interval normalized hinge stress: PASS

The root read `candidate 95c59f781b5c15f4`.
Its constraints have a common finite closed polyhedral partition. Near a
feasible point only cells containing that point occur; Hoffman bounds can
therefore be applied to nonempty cell-feasible intersections. The exact
penalty produces objective multiplier one. Convex combinations of dual
optimal interval coverage certificates remain dual optimal, and any primal
minimizer forms a saddle pair with them. Thus the contact selected for the
stress is an actual interval point. This argument is confined to d=1.

## New selector and flow certificates: PASS

The root read `candidate 5939c45de14c2bb5` and
`candidate 121d9e12ac57cde9` in full, and ran their
exact verifiers. Both pass. The first optimizes over all dominated interval
submeasures, not merely uniform thinning, and its alternative-t analysis
does not claim to refute optimizing the mass parameter. The second accounts
for all oblique slopes and vertical boundary-fiber caps. The root independently
derived its piecewise depth formula before reading the saved proof.

The residual-centroid obstruction's verifier also passes. Its entire selector
class stays above the fixed first-coordinate threshold of an already certified
bad ambient cap. This is a failure of that rule, not of the available points
elsewhere in the middle fiber.

## Exposed-fiber compression and n=1 interpolation: PASS

The root read `candidate 25f2a08c9ca43383` and
`candidate f7422e63e37f7d98` in full. The
minimax/Caratheodory extraction, removal of null caps by closure, median
replacement, and local-to-global hinge accounting all check. The parity
count requires both convex position and lattice convexity, as stated.

The root supplied the n=1 interpolation argument independently. It extends
without change to all nonempty compact convex fibers, including varying
affine dimensions, since it uses only support functions. That strengthening
is incorporated in the file. Its comparison bodies must be formed after
the exact replacement C by conv(S); the real-bulge example explains why.
The common affine section is extended to R^n before its shear is used.

All results retain their stated limitations. The complete all-n, all-d OC
goal remains active and unproved.

## Actual integer-centroid interval cases and angular reduction: PASS

The root read both the four- and five-fiber arguments in full, including
every captured-subset case, the Jensen inequalities at the central fiber,
and the endpoint-elimination coefficients. The separate degeneracy audit
checked 17 expanded polynomial identities and all integer-mean locations.
These are finite-case theorems under exactly their stated centroid hypothesis.

The root also read the complete angular-minimum reduction. Every nonvertical
cap mass is a continuous piecewise affine function of slope, with constant
tails at both infinities. These finite plateaus strictly dominate vertical
closed caps because the central interval is properly cut. Convexity bounds
endpoint coincidences by two. The nine-row derivative table and each flat
perturbation producing a symmetric proper block check directly. No boundary
mass is discarded. The exceptional upward/upward cusp captures no whole
fiber. This proof does not estimate the captured tails.

## Affine contact graph and unnormalized parallel growth: PASS

The root read the affine-root-majorant contact theorem. The majorant is
global over every nonempty integer fiber, and its equality chain forces
both the Brunn--Minkowski equality case and equality in the majorant at
every receiving integer fiber. Intrinsic directions are forced equal
before the equality theorem is used. The weighted graph conclusion retains
the exact contact-mass fraction.

The root read the common-addition growth theorem. Minkowski sums of each
old cap with the centroid cap of the added body stay in the corresponding
new cap for every ambient normal. The case of zero old cap mass uses the
translated added-body centroid cap in the selected point's fiber. The
sum-of-powers step and passage to a supremum need no unproved maximizer.
The statement uses full d-volume and makes no intrinsic-limit claim.

## Additional root checks in the twenty-second synthesis

Read the complete adjacent-integer convex partition proof. Its top-mass
integer marginal feasibility and equality cases are correct, the strict
fractional source supplies an actual coercive norm, and the prescribed
nonzero continuous normal makes every final boundary mixed-null. Zero
volume fibers can remain and convex cap centroid membership is actual.
Read the John-root supergradient proof (Section 8): normalization, John
trace inequality, singleton targets, and strict positivity of the
majorant on compact Q_t all follow as written.

Read the generic-budget hinge note through Section 7. Semialgebraic
clipped-polytope moments use a finite rational triangulation, not false
closure of arbitrary integrals. The uniform offset repair is exact.
Two local penalties suffice for normality; the LP saddle-feature
representation correctly keeps a finite contact measure. Independent
boundary/gradient audit is still pending. No mass inequality is inferred.

Constructed and verified an exact obstruction to maximizing raw moment
width over source mass: widths(2,16,17,1). Simultaneous two-source QP
certificates prove all base optimizers; every associated midpoint has a
strictly bad ambient cap. Fraction verifier passed. This closes that
new selector without relying on numerical evidence.

## Whole-space rank reduction and covariance normalization

Read the whole-space framed and unframed rank-stratum notes. The minimal
normal face supports every balanced certificate. Removing its outside
zero-cost caps and parameterizing the retained span with individual unit
normals plus a common rotation gives local coercivity without added caps.
Projected individual equations and common-rotation stationarity combine
into the stated full source tensor. Rank1 exclusion uses the same positive
fiber integer convexity already present in actual C. Independent audit of
the full open-complement Helly reduction is pending.

Read candidate a5bd7e36a76479fe
and ran supporting computation verify_residual_covariance_simplex_obstruction.py: PASS. The allowed
regression/shear covariance bookkeeping is correct, including singular
base covariance and positive definite continuous residual covariance.
Simplex facet covariance identities give the exact canonical normal stress
with r=0 for all simplex products. The two equal-area anisotropic triangles
have the stated common residual covariance and tangent defect -2/135;
canonical sharp-budget six-cap classification keeps every other-fiber
section multiplier out of this equation. This closes the proposed universal
covariance fix of endpoint normality. It does not contradict generic-budget
normality and does not give an OC counterexample.

Read the raw-moment John theorem through its original Section7. Unique
support source indicators at all feasible constraints make interpolation
strict; harmonic source weights preserve an integer averaged base despite
unequal masses. The augmented contact-cone separation correctly retains
the mass slope and gives sum lambda b=0, then sum lambda Psi=d. The added
endpoint deletion lemma is awaiting the independent audit. None of these
geometric facts reinstates the disproved raw-John midpoint selector.

## Twenty-fifth synthesis: rank, density and quantitative contacts

the contributor read candidate f9c635ce5abe9f17 in full.
The quantile/Hölder radial proof works when the support ray begins away
from zero; the critical inverse exponent is correctly tracked. The
deepest-point active-normal argument uses uniform positive slab mass,
then radial cap preservation, and does not identify the radial origin
with a centroid. Central projection keeps the t^(d-1) Jacobian. Boundary
contacts use simultaneous translations and a finite fixed-index limit.
Full-rank sharpness is explicitly an infimum, not exact equality at
positive perturbation. PASS.

the contributor read candidate a20765b75f4bd3ee and
near-grunbaum-budget-common-contact-centroid-rigidity.md. Convex truncation
keeps mass (1-delta)W and makes the same contact a boundary point; the
inner symmetry calculation has the correct direction. The quantitative
proof's two-cone bound p<=d, log-density entropy bound p(mean)>=1, and
centroid slab gain all hold for general convex bodies, including facets.
Translating by a boundary vector of K-K indeed makes the contact external
or boundary, and the support-function inclusion is in the stated polar
direction. The exact displayed modulus follows. PASS; independent audit
requested separately.

the contributor wrote rank-sensitive-continuous-cap-cover-theorem.md. The exact
projected marginal obeys the necessary negative-power convexity, and the
external density proof applies without assuming log-concavity of the
central projection. The depth agent independently audited the proof:

cover lower constants depend only on the normal rank.

the contributor read candidate 203262a6491295f6 through
its original Section4. Distinct original source indices are necessary
for the bound sum c_jz<=T and are explicitly required. The lifted
normal map is injective and preserves rank. Its common-flat incidence
uses a surjective linear image of actual interiors, not just closures.
Positive proper strips and negative tails give the asserted strictly
positive union defect. The heavy-fiber conclusion retains the strict
versus weak threshold cases. PASS; it is not an aggregate mass bound.

the contributor read the conditional Schwarz and localization-obstruction notes.
All real slices, including zero-radius nonempty ones, are retained.
Restricted-function equality and the Clarke composition inclusion permit
a physical gradient lift; reflection averaging inside the convex gradient
set removes the unused components. This avoids transporting arbitrary
unrealizable traces. The intrinsic counterexample and tensor obstruction
are correctly scoped. Ran supporting computation verify_schwarz_single_level_tensor_obstruction.py
using work/math-venv/bin/python: PASS.

the contributor read both sampled-projective radial counterexamples and ran
supporting computation verify_sampled_projective_ball_nonconvexity.py and
supporting computation verify_sampled_ball_dilation_obstruction.py in the same venv: PASS.
The initial system-python invocation could not import sympy; it was an
environment failure, followed by the successful existing-venv run, not
a mathematical test failure. Deepest-anchor and arbitrary-anchor scopes
are kept separate. None is an OC counterexample.

## Follow-up audits: intrinsic fibers, strict interpolation and section induction

the contributor read the full rank-sensitive localization proof. Its comparison
point is an actual deepest point of the projected marginal, not its
centroid. Unimodality and the two nontrivial tails give p(t*)>=alpha;
the scalar ambient section exponent then gives the asserted slab gain.
The two dimensions r and D occur in the correct separate places. PASS.

the contributor wrote the full-fiber Doignon theorem and read degeneracy's direct
intrinsic extension. The maximal-dimension base set P is integer convex
even when fiber directions vary: an integer Minkowski interpolation
has dimension at least q and cannot exceed the global maximum q.
The same argument for relatively open strictly negative pieces proves
integer convexity of the positive-uncaptured-remainder base set. Whole
fibers on a closed cap boundary are correctly counted as captured. The
finite Doignon application is legitimate for the compact hulls, includes
empty hulls, and provides a subfamily of ORIGINAL caps. All H_q fiber
sums and q=0 are explicit. Independent audit PASS.

the contributor read candidate 9afb6a8708a420d7 fully.
Positive-depth endpoints lie in their fiber interiors by finite roof
LP duality. Integer-tilt saturation yields an attained nonvertical cap.
Any equality cap must contain both endpoints on its boundary. Its
proper section indices are all interior indices of the real section
projection; only the two extremes may have optional supporting traces.
One-sided derivatives supply consistent weights in [0,s_z], and the
log-concave likelihood-ratio calculation bounds their mean range by
one. The contradiction is valid for any intermediate integer index.
No multidimensional lattice aggregation was used. PASS; functional's
separate independent audit also PASS.

the contributor read candidate 203262a6491295f6 Section5
and the full aggregate-light-fiber obstruction. Strict product defects
do exclude nonvertex contacts in the threshold heavy-fiber hull. The
new aggregate example instead has individually light fibers; its one
circuit misses the heavy bottom layer completely. It is not a global
bad cover. Its cap fractions, barycentric weights, integer tilt and
exact convolution signs were verified by the supplied exact script:

margin scale.

the contributor read the inverse-convex target/minorant obstruction in full and
ran its Fraction verifier: PASS. The all-coupling cap certificate
remains valid with boundary mass. The new retained-mass bound follows
directly from any gamma_2 centerpoint property and domination. The
boundedness proof for an integrable inverse-power-convex density uses
an actual interpolated interior ball and has the correct epsilon^-1
mass divergence. It does not claim arbitrary target measures fail.

the contributor caught a degeneracy gap in the first section-induction draft:
an original zero-d-volume fiber can have positive (d-1)-dimensional
section measure, while the stress only imposes coverage at positive
original bases. The corrected proof first intersects with conv(P) in
the base and then reduces its saturated integer affine span by a
unimodular transformation. the contributor read that correction. All retained
fiber cap functions and derivative integrals are unchanged; every
new section base is covered. The true inductive constant is
gamma_(d-1)/2^m, with m<=n. The explicit discarded-base example checks
the need for this repair. The corrected exact verifier PASS.

The remaining pure-section equations and the triangle-cluster Clarke
trace counterexample check as stated. Arbitrary effective traces are
not uniform convex-section measures, even when their barycenter lies
in the section. The checkerboard endpoint permits a legitimate pure
abnormal stress with zero multiplied section measure. Neither example
is a below-target complete cap cover. No induction closure is inferred.

the contributor read multidimensional-section-barycenter-parity-and-strict-depth-
obstruction.md completely. The four actual nearby gradient patterns
produce the exact stated trace, so the barycenter certificate is
consistent. The downward cap proof uses a valid two-face gain pairing
and convex maximization of the untruncated ternary-cube loss; its
constant102 and resulting margin22 check. Upward-face pairing and the
vertical limit retain boundary mass. The T>=1 extension preserves
the unnormalized minimum82 while total mass increases; at T=5 the
below-OC inequality is exact. The deeper center's symmetric submeasure
proves these candidates are NOT global maximizers. The higher-d
extension asserts only section stationarity and strict local minimum,
not the unproved all-halfspace depth formula in those dimensions.
Ran supporting computation verify_multidimensional_section_barycenter_parity.py: PASS.
Degeneracy's independent full audit also PASS. This closes the broad
candidate-level parity statement, not its global-maximizer variant.

the contributor read candidate f2d1fbdd5a877f5b and
its critical-cover dependency through the exact finite-cover proof.
The base-functional flux is the pointwise sharp maximization of
theta_1(h-1)-theta_0 h. The ambient extension has the correct opposite
one-sided derivatives on full and empty supporting caps; proper
sections and null faces are handled without assigning them arbitrary
mass. The critical cover is a proved finite CLOSED cover at the exact
depth, not an assumed finite representation of the entire Tukey region.
Caps through a global midpoint yield an actual full continuous-space
cover near its own fiber interior and hence a positive normal circuit.
The base-affine shear preserves every fiber volume and the lattice.
the contributor made its distinct-base hypothesis explicit after the independent
degeneracy audit requested that scope clarification. Both audits PASS;
supporting computation verify_equal_depth_facet_flux.py PASS. Arbitrary faceted global plateaus
remain unexcluded. No bound summing their exterior facet flux into
the OC constant has been proved.

## Additional root audit: strict approximants, oriented flux, and contraction

Read the complete outer-strict-convex approximation and compatibility-slack
notes. PASS: the explicit squared ball-radius excess is positive, finite
candidate integer bases and outer containment give convergence also at
boundary slices, and normalized total-variation control plus enlarged
closed halfspaces preserves one center and boundary mass. The intrinsic
diagonal controls outer mass error relative to each tube's positive mass.
Representation-polytope vertices give uniform Minkowski slack only after
removing the target coefficient; support functions justify exact perturbed
fiber containment. Perpendicular base thickening creates no new integer
fibers when chosen below the finite positive distance list. Both independent
agent audits also PASS. No strict-class attainment is inferred.

Read candidate e81d0f726880ea4a and the empty-face
transfer note. PASS: right derivative at endpoint1 minus left derivative at
endpoint0 is -A+E*dist-F*(1+dist). The finite weighted balanced sum retains
all labeled face measures. The layered-cube opposite-cap obstruction has
the stated positive left side and zero right side. The exact verifier
passes. Positive-local-volume caps alone cover each positive fiber by
closedness, but their traces on an empty face need not resemble their own
sections; the explicit triangle has face2 and section sum4epsilon.

The new root maximizing-hull note was independently audited PASS by the
functional agent. Its uniform negative margin proof retains the other
maximum's finite tilt evaluation exactly during saturation; no uniform
bound over different bodies or faceted-limit parity claim is used.

Read candidate a57c113e8e14cc38 and
ran supporting computation verify_nonvertex_fiber_deletion_depth.py: PASS. Removing one nonvertex
generator preserves every retained fiber, and reinstating its interpolant
changes exactly that fiber. Extending depth to all Lambda handles removed
centers: outside the smaller convex body its depth is zero by strict
separation. Thus 0<=A_C-A_D<=mass(C)-mass(D) is valid. The interval all-slope
formula gives beta(b)=(b+5)/(4(b+2)) for1<=b<=3 and (b+1)/(2(b+2)) for b>=3;
the certified contraction values1/2,2/5,3/7 refute normalized monotonicity
and quasiconcavity. This is an above-target auxiliary obstruction only.

Read quantitative-uncaptured-fiber-doignon-threshold.md. the contributor check PASS:
positive strict-negative remainders have common q-dimensional direction
spaces whenever their combination lands at an integer base, so intrinsic
Brunn--Minkowski gives integer-convex absoluteresearch-agent thresholds. The strict
sum in the water-level Doignon contradiction is justified by at least one
w_z>t*, since F(t*)=2^n B>0. Centroid coverage yields an actual proper cut,
and both the explicit W-bound and the implicit B-bound track gamma_q.
Relative fractions are not assumed convex. Independent functional audit
was requested separately before adding this as an audited dependency.

## the contributor audit: genuinely global plateaus and the parameter construction

Read candidate 5cb6b3de949f5208 in full,
including the paired-threshold and all-dimensional extensions. PASS.
The seven lower interval pieces and three upper pieces have disjoint
receiving labels/ranges. Lower projected displacements are nonnegative;
each adverse upper displacement is4a-6/5, giving the exact tail error.
The two middle leftovers and symmetric block give the claimed all-tilt
lower bound24. Global upper covers, excluded other d1 maximizers, and
vertical closed boundary mass all check. The paired b-c,b+c tail terms
cancel with the correct signs, and the saturated two-term clamp lower
bound is valid for every real c. Integration against a symmetric convex
factor is therefore authorized by a proved inequality. Zero x coefficients
use bounded upper-Fatou in the correct direction. Exact verifier PASS;
independent degeneracy and functional extension audits PASS.

the contributor then originated the parameter extension and read the saved complete
note unbounded-number-of-global-maximizing-bases.md. PASS. For INTEGER s>=1,
the explicit three-piece target injection uses distinct indices0..6s+2,
inside the available bottom range -8s-4..6s+4. Middle leftover count is2s
with index sum s(8s+5). The decisive coefficient is exactly3s+2, and the
large-tilt surplus is2. Mixed mass72s+44 and critical cap mass24s+14 match
the four-cap cover. Quasiconcavity gives at least2s+1 actual global centers;
no exact global-set assertion is required. Paired thresholds and all closed
ambient halfspaces are proved as above. Verifier PASS and BOTH independent
full parameter audits PASS. All depths exceed OC; only the unconditioned
global parity/count auxiliary hypotheses are refuted.

Read concave-remainder-profiles-local-fraction-coverage-obstruction.md.
PASS after the functional agent's necessary correction of root's initial
tilt coefficient:1-c^2 replaces gamma_d in general d. The actual fibers
cT,T,cT have mass(3-2gamma)|T|; caps have masses gamma|T| and
gamma(1-gamma)|T|. All real-base remainder roots are concave with the stated
slopes, each fiber has a cap capturing fraction gamma, yet the entire
(z,0) line is missed. Thus the scalar data cannot replace genuine coverage.
The exact algebra proves all d>=2; finite verifier checks are supplementary.

Full OC resolution remains absent. No proved lemma or audited certificate
in this checkpoint supplies the missing arbitrary-unequal-fiber sharp
global mass allocation, and the goal must not be marked complete.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
